teachingQuestion: What must be decided before, during, and after a privileged communication channel is opened?
focalInsight: A secure channel is governed end to end: authorize and constrain it before use, protect and observe it during use, and revoke and evidence it afterward.
title: Privileged channel lifecycle
caption: Authorize and validate the protected path before granting privileged access; close the scoped access and retain appropriate evidence.

nodes.label: Request and purpose
nodes.detail: Identify the actor, business purpose, target service and support or collaboration need. Provider maintenance needs explicit scope and accountable sponsorship.

nodes.label: Approve scope and window
nodes.detail: Approve the identity, privilege, time window and intended path. Voice/video use also needs suitable recording consent, access and retention governance.

nodes.label: Check endpoints and termination
nodes.detail: Check protocol endpoints, authentication, key/certificate trust, encryption termination, exposed metadata and any onward hop; a protected link alone is not end-to-end service assurance.

nodes.label: Enforce the permitted session
nodes.detail: Grant resource access only after the approved identity, channel and authorization checks succeed. Broker remote administration through the approved path, with bounded privileges.

nodes.label: Observe use and constraints
nodes.detail: Monitor relevant actions and session state; preserve accountable logs without collecting secrets or recording communications beyond the approved purpose.

nodes.label: Revoke and verify
nodes.detail: End the session and revoke time-bounded grants at completion or expiry. Verify closure, investigate unexpected persistence and retain the authorized record. A later purpose is a new access decision.

altSummary: Six steps separate purpose and approval, endpoint/termination validation, permitted session enforcement, observation, and verified revocation; later work requires a new decision.
